answer.rationale:
The decisive memory is memory_c2 (the prior low-cost switch that cut unit cost with quick onboarding), because it is the only record that would justify flipping primary supply on a 14-day clock. I want its archived source to check the conditions it was earned under: was that component constrained, was the line running with slack, and what volume share actually moved? A cheap, clean onboarding at low share with buffer inventory says almost nothing about moving primary supply for a component feeding a line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. If c2 turns out to be a non-constrained, low-share switch, the apparent 'proven' path collapses into an untested one.

On current evidence the price mandate is real (incumbent has refused to reopen, so memory_c4's renegotiation lever and memory_c6's multi-year lever are both closed this cycle) and memory_c5's defer path is not available: the contract does not auto-renew and there is no buffer, so deferral converts a cost problem into a stockout. That leaves cost pressure pushing toward the low-cost vendor and risk pressure pushing against an unhedged single-vendor flip. memory_c3 is the closest structural match to the present constraint: dual sourcing held allocation through a shortage.

So I intend to add the low-cost vendor as a qualified second source at small guarded scale, a limited share with a short bridge on the incumbent, rather than a full switch. This buys the price evidence and the qualification data I do not yet have, while keeping the line covered.

Risks I am flagging rather than resolving: (1) a partial second source likely does not deliver the full 18% cut this year, so finance's target may slip to the next review and this decision should not be reported as satisfying the mandate; (2) the bridge on the incumbent may be unavailable or priced punitively given they have already refused to move, which would force a harder choice next cycle; (3) if verification shows c2 covered a genuinely comparable constrained, high-utilization component at meaningful share, the case for a fuller switch strengthens and I would revisit scale. I am not treating the low-cost vendor's quoted price as a demonstrated landed cost until qualification returns actual delivery and quality data.
